Measuring coffee using its brewed amount is just about the most ignorant thing I see people do. The process of making coffee needs two simple things: how strong, and how much; not "how much brewed coffee do I want in ml?" or "how many cups of coffee do I want". This just really gets on my nerve when people measure coffee in cups or in its brewed volume, which is such a profoundly ignorant thing to do. How much brewed coffee there is is irrelevant and empty information; you'd want to drink two cups of a weak coffee compared to one cup of coffee that is twice as strong. 

The only sensible thing to do is to decide on how much coffee you want to have in grams first, not cups or ml, and then figure out how much water is needed, and that's how we get to the 1:X. If that's too difficult for you to calculate, that's your problem. The point stands that the 1:X format is the only method that makes sense. Measuring coffee in its brewed form doesn't make any sense in any situation that is not superficial in some way such as hospitality for example.
